policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ἐγκακοῦμεν and ἐκκακοῦμεν are orthographic variants of the same verb; ASV 'we faint not' renders either identically and no note is mapped here.
συνιστάνοντες/συνιστάντες/συνιστῶντες are alternative present participle formations of the same verb; ASV 'commending ourselves' renders all three identically.

ASV 'should not dawn upon them' carries an unitalicized 'upon them' answering to the dative αὐτοῖς; the base reading leaves the object unexpressed, and ASV italicizes supplied words. The marginal 'that they should not see the light . . . image of God' is classed alternative_rendering and concerns the construal of subject and object, not the presence of αὐτοῖς.

ASV 'but Christ Jesus as Lord' preserves the order Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν; the transposed Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν would give 'Jesus Christ'. The mapped note ('Some ancient authorities read through Jesus') bears on a different variation, not this order.
ASV 'Light shall shine out of darkness' is a future indicative, rendering λάμψει; the aorist infinitive λάμψαι would yield an imperatival 'Let light shine'.
ASV 'in the face of Jesus Christ' renders Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ; the base Χριστοῦ alone would give 'of Christ', and 'Jesus' is not italicized.
ASV 'the dying of Jesus' has no 'the Lord'; the added κυρίου would give 'of the Lord Jesus', as ASV renders it where it stands (4:14).
The correlative μέν is regularly left unrendered in ASV; 'So then death worketh in us, but life in you' answers to the δέ clause alone and is compatible with or without μέν.

ASV text reads 'he that raised up the Lord Jesus' with the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit the Lord', so κύριον stands in the text and the omission is relegated to the margin.
ASV 'shall raise up us also with Jesus' renders σὺν Ἰησοῦ; διὰ Ἰησοῦ would give 'through Jesus' (which ASV notes at 4:5 as an 'ancient authorities' reading elsewhere, not here).
ἐγκακοῦμεν and ἐκκακοῦμεν are orthographic variants of the same verb; ASV 'we faint not' renders either identically.
ASV 'our inward man' has an unitalicized possessive matching ἡμῶν in ὁ ἔσω ἡμῶν; ἔσωθεν alone ('the man from within') supplies no pronoun and ASV italicizes supplied words.
ASV 'our light affliction' renders τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν with an unitalicized 'our'; the omission would leave 'the light affliction', and the separate 'for us' answers to ἡμῖν later in the verse.
